newsitem.title: UK: British Aero to end Jetstream 41 production.
newsitem.headline: British Aero to end Jetstream 41 production.

text.p: British Aerospace announced on Thursday it would finally end production of its Jetstream 41 turboprop aircraft by the end of this year.
The aircraft manufacturing giant said it was getting out of building the 30-seat aircraft as a crowded market was resulting in poor pricing and profitability.
The group said in a statement that up to 380 jobs would be lost after it stopped production.

The group would make a net provision of 250 million pounds ($409.1 million), after taking account of a deferred tax credit of 80 million pounds, in the accounts for the first half of 1997 for costs of ceasing Jetstream 41 production and the associated reorganisation.
The cash cost of this action will be about 220 million pounds of which about 120 million will be incurred by the end of 1998.
The share price of the company was up 17 pence to 1,239 3/4p shortly after the announcement was made.
British Aerospace, however, said it remained committed to its Prestwick facility and would take a number of actions to attract additional aerostructures work to the site.
